newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanbo Steel auction postponed, no bids.
newsitem.headline: Hanbo Steel auction postponed, no bids.

text.p: An auction to sell the failed Hanbo Steel Co was postponed until around the end of this month because no offers had been submitted, Korea First Bank said on Monday.
The deadline to submit applications to bid for Hanbo was 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT) on Monday. The auction was originally set for July 8.
"No companies showed up. We will now set a date for the next auction," said Kang Won-kyung, an official in the public relations department of Korea First, Hanbo's main creditor.
Analysts said they had expected no one to bid for Hanbo Steel unless the takeover terms were improved.
"It's not surprising at all. It's not sensible (a good decision) to take over Hanbo at the current conditions," said Lee Hwa-yeol at financial analyst at Ssangyong Securities.
"The issue cannot be solved overnight," said Peter Lee, steel analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities. "Unless conditions improved drastically, the auction will continue to be postponed."

The Korea First Bank said earlier potential buyers must indicate going-concern value of Hanbo Steel as well as their estimates of Hanbo's liabilities and assets. An accounting company commissioned to evaluate the steelmaker estimated its liabilities at 6.61 trillion won, compared to assets of 4.97 trillion. The steel mill, capable of producing six million tonnes of steel annually, is 90 percent completed.
Under qualifications set out by creditor banks, only 17 business conglomerates are deemed eligible to take part in the auction.
The creditors have ruled that any participant must have shareholders' equity worth one trillion won or more, and minimum assets and annual turnover of 10 trillion won each.
Hyundai Group and 10 other conglomerates including Samsung and LG attended a briefing session on the auction on July 1.
"The current requirements will not be eased in the next auction," Kang said.
The Korea First Bank has said any buyer of Hanbo Steel would have to repay the liabilities over five years after a 10-year grace period.
Annual interest on the liabilities would be 8.5 percent during the grace period and 11.5 percent thereafter.
Scott Seo, banking analyst at Deutche Morgan Grenfell Capital Markets Ltd, predicted that creditors would have to ease their requirements to sell off Hanbo Steel.
Many analysts have said they believed Hyundai Group is the only potential buyer of the troubled steelmaker. But Hyundai has repeatedly said it is was not interested in the purchase.
Banking analysts said the delay in the auction was not expected to have any impact on shares of creditor banks.
